name: Abdul-Rakhman Yakhyaev
summary: Unbeaten 25-year-old Chechen-born light heavyweight (10-0, 3-0 UFC) with a combat sambo base who trains at MMA Nuernberg and with Fight Sports in Florida. All three UFC wins and his Contender Series win came in round one: 33-second RNC of Raffael Cerqueira, RNC of Brendson Ribeiro, and an 8-second KO of Julius Walker. Not yet tested past the first round in the UFC.

how_they_fight.Striking: Explosive starter who throws spinning kicks, head kicks and a heavy right hand from the opening bell; the Walker KO was a right hand over the lead shoulder at 0:08. Long reach (about 198 cm) for the division.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Strongest suit: sambo/wrestling base, quick takedowns off strikes, ground-and-pound and fast back takes; 5 career submissions (4 in R1). Took Ribeiro down after being hit, then took the back for the RNC.
how_they_fight.Defense: The gap: overly aggressive starts. Ribeiro landed a high kick and a right hand that nearly cost him (per LowKick), and he ate another shot while shooting; he admitted taking more punches than planned (UFC.com).
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Extreme fast starter: 8 of 9 finishes in R1, one sub in R2. Only one fight past round two, a five-round decision over Nikolay Kovalenko (Khan Fight, 2023), so cardio over 15 minutes at UFC level is largely unknown. Never been stopped.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Decisive and confident; recovers quickly from adversity by switching to grappling. Wants to stay very active and calls fighting 'like a drug' (UFC.com).

patterns: Blitz from the opening bell; R1 finishes (8 of 9)
Strikes to level change; back takes and RNC
Responds to being hit by shooting and grappling
Little UFC data beyond five minutes
concerns: Hittable on entries early (Ribeiro clipped him twice)
Untested in deep waters at UFC level
Step up in experience against a 43-fight veteran
keys_to_beat: Survive the first round and make him work late

news.text: Made weight at the official weigh-ins: 206 lb (Krylov 206).
Sherdog preview: -520 favourite (Krylov +390); picks him by first-round KO, doubting Krylov gets the time to grind as he did against Bukauskas.
KO'd Julius Walker in 8 seconds at UFC Baku; earned Performance of the Night.
Booked against Nikita Krylov at UFC 333, a big step up per Cageside Press; no injury or camp news found.
